# Overview {.unnumbered}

**Harvard's TinyTorch** is to Machine Learning Systems what MIT's xv6 was to Operating Systems: the first transparent, builder-first reference implementation where every layer of the modern ML stack is built from scratch and demystified.

Building systems creates irreversible understanding. In this volume, we move beyond calling high-level library functions (`import torch`) to construct the entire ML systems runtime from first principles—from linear memory buffers, dynamic automatic differentiation, and multi-head attention to kernel vectorization, INT8 quantization, and KV-cache inference memoization.

| Part | Focus & Scope | Key Systems Deliverables |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Part I: Foundations & Core Engine** | Memory, derivatives, optimization | `Storage`, `Tensor`, `GELU`, `Linear`, `CrossEntropyLoss`, `AutogradTape`, `AdamW`, `DataLoader` |
| **Part II: Deep Architectures** | Spatial compute, subwords, transformers | `Conv2d` (im2col), `BPETokenizer`, `Embedding`, `MultiHeadAttention`, `TransformerBlock`, `TinyGPT` |
| **Part III: Systems Acceleration** | Hardware profiling, compression, caching | Williams Roofline model, INT8 Quantization, SVD Pruning, Fused Kernels, `KVCache`, MLPerf Benchmarks |
| **Part IV: Capstone & Frontiers** | End-to-end evaluation & modern runtimes | Torch Olympics multi-metric leaderboard, OpenAI Triton block programming, TorchInductor JIT |

Everything in this book is built in readable, dependency-free Python using only NumPy for raw 1D buffer allocation. Every module is accompanied by formal unit tests, benchmarks, and production sidebars bridging our minimal implementation to production C++ (`c10::TensorImpl`) and CUDA runtimes.
